name: Tallinn Zoo
description: Estonia's only zoo has wide paved paths that work well with a stroller and plenty of big animals for a toddler to point at. In winter the indoor exhibitions and the Children's Zoo barn give you warm breaks between outdoor loops.
tips: Pre-school children get in free with the paying adult, so a toddler visit costs only the adult or family ticket.

price.note: Winter prices (gate); online tickets EUR 1 cheaper. Summer: adult 19, family 38. Pre-school children free with a paying adult; family ticket covers up to 2 adults and children up to 19.

discounts: Family ticket (2 adults + children up to 19)
Free entry for under-19s on Children's Saturdays (2nd Saturday, Nov-Apr; check dates)
Combined family ticket with Open Air Museum
hours: Daily 9:00-17:00 in winter (ticket office until 16:00); indoor exhibitions Mon 11:00-16:00, Tue-Sun 10:00-16:00; hours change by season

name: Children's Zoo at Tallinn Zoo
description: A small farm-animal corner inside the zoo, with goats and other domestic animals at toddler eye level. In winter the animals live in a barn you can walk through, so it still works on cold days.
tips: The barn is closed on the last Monday of each month for cleaning, and the goat yard shuts in bad or very cold weather.

price.note: Included in the Tallinn Zoo ticket.

hours: Daily 10:00-17:00 (barn); closed last Monday of the month

name: Children's Museum Miiamilla
description: A hands-on children's museum in Kadriorg Park with role-play rooms and things to touch, open, and climb. It's aimed mostly at preschoolers, but a confident walker will find plenty to do too.
tips: You need a time-slot ticket for everyone, including free babies, and on weekends tickets are sold only online in advance.

price.note: Child EUR 6 from age 3; under-2s free but still need a booked ticket. Family = up to 2 adults + children under 19. Visits capped at 2 hours. The city museum page says under-3s are free, so the cut-off is unclear.

discounts: Free with Tallinn Card (booking still needed)
hours: Sep-May: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat-Sun 10:00-17:00; Jun-Aug: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00; closed Mon

name: Seaplane Harbour (Lennusadam)
description: A huge maritime museum in old seaplane hangars, with a real submarine, boats, and lots of open floor for a toddler to wander. Outside you can visit the Suur Tõll icebreaker on the same ticket.
tips: Food and drink can't be brought inside, so plan snacks before or after.

price.note: Combined ticket (hangar, exhibition, Suur Tõll, Valvas); child price for ages 9-18. Free for young children (official page says 8 and under). New prices from 1 Jan 2026. Family = 1-2 adults + minors.

discounts: Seaplane Harbour + Fat Margaret combined ticket
hours: Oct-Apr: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; May-Sep: daily 10:00-19:00; ticket sales end 30 min before closing

name: Kumu Art Museum
description: Estonia's main art museum is a big, airy modern building where a toddler can look at colourful works while you have a quieter, warm outing. It runs family programmes, but those are aimed at 4-8 year olds, so with a 1-2 year old treat it as a slow stroll.
tips: The family ticket allows one visit within a year of purchase, so you can buy it ahead and go on a bad-weather day.

price.note: Discount ticket EUR 11 (students, seniors 65+, pupils). Family = up to 2 adults + their underage children. Free age for small children not confirmed.

hours: Tue, Thu-Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed 10:00-20:00; closed Mon (check seasonal changes)

name: Kadriorg Park
description: Tallinn's grandest park has paved paths for strollers, the Swan Pond, and flower gardens that are nice for a slow walk with a napping baby. Cafés, toilets, and playgrounds are spread around the park, so it's easy to stay for half a day.
tips: Pair a park walk with Miiamilla or Kumu on the same trip, as all three are a few minutes apart.

price.note: Park entry is free.

name: Kadriorg Children's Park playground
address: Next to Lydia Koidula 21c (Miiamilla), Kadriorg, Tallinn
description: A large historic playground beside the Miiamilla museum, with a sandy area where little ones can dig and a famous old blue slide. It's one of the playgrounds most often recommended for the smallest children.
tips: Bring sand toys; the city plans a rebuild (finish targeted for summer 2028), so check for short closures.

price.note: Free public playground.

name: Tallinn Botanic Garden
description: Big outdoor gardens and forest paths for summer, plus a warm Palm House and greenhouses that make a good winter outing with a toddler. Paths are mostly calm and spacious, with picnic areas for snack breaks.
tips: The Palm House is closed on the last Monday of each month.

price.note: Discount (pupils, students, pensioners) EUR 5; family = up to 2 adults + children up to 19; Family Card holders EUR 9. Ticket page about 7 months old; free age for toddlers not confirmed.

hours: Winter (Oct-Apr): outdoor gardens 9:00-20:00, greenhouses/Palm House 11:00-16:00, visitor centre 10:00-16:00

name: Pirita Beach
description: Tallinn's longest sandy beach has children's playgrounds, changing cabins, and lifeguards in summer. The shallow sand is great for a toddler with a bucket and spade, and the pine woods behind it give shade.
tips: Lifeguards are on duty in summer 9:00-20:00 on weekdays and 9:00-21:00 at weekends, so pick those hours for paddling.

price.note: Free public beach.

hours: Open all the time; lifeguards in summer

name: Stroomi Beach Park
description: A locals' beach in northern Tallinn with shallow water, a playground, and long paved paths for strollers. Outdoor cafés and an ice-cream truck in summer make it easy to stay a while.
tips: Water quality is said to be a bit lower than at Pirita, so check the city's bathing water notices before swimming.

price.note: Free public beach and park.

name: Toompark and Snelli Pond
description: A green park right under the Old Town walls, built around the last surviving piece of the old moat. It's a short, flat loop with ducks to watch, ideal for a quick stroller walk between city errands.
tips: In winter the pond is a popular skating spot, which toddlers love to watch from the path.

price.note: Free public park.

name: Löwenruh Park
description: A four-hectare park around a round pond with several playgrounds, including one built to be accessible. Visitors describe a big play structure with options for different ages, plus easy paths for strollers.

price.note: Free public park.

name: Kalamaja Park
description: A former cemetery turned into a leafy local park in the Kalamaja neighbourhood, popular with families for a quiet walk. It's a handy stop if you're spending the day in Kalamaja or at the Seaplane Harbour.

price.note: Free public park.

name: Estonian Open Air Museum and Farm Kid's World
description: A big seaside park of old farmhouses, windmills, and forest paths, with Farm Kid's World offering domestic animals and an outdoor adventure trail for small children. It's a full day out with lots of space for a toddler to explore.
tips: Children up to 8 get in free, and Farm Kid's World is only open Thursday to Sunday in winter.

price.note: Winter season (29 Sep-22 Apr) prices; summer adult 18, family 38. Children up to 8 free. Family = up to 2 adults + children under 19.

discounts: Combined family ticket with Tallinn Zoo (EUR 40 winter, EUR 55 summer)
hours: Winter: Tue-Sun, park 10:00-19:00, buildings 10:00-17:00; Farm Kid's World Thu-Sun 10:00-16:00

name: Tallinn Central Library, Südalinna branch
description: The central library's main building has a parent-and-baby room with a changing table, sink, and armchair for feeding, which makes it a calm city-centre stop with a little one. Children up to 7 can get a free library card under the 'Born to Be a Reader' programme.
tips: Ask about the free library card for children under 7, which comes with a keepsake card pocket.

price.note: Free entry; free reader's card for children up to 7.

discounts: Free library card for children up to 7

name: Kalamaja Library toddler mornings
description: A small neighbourhood library that has run 'põnnihommik' (toddler mornings) with stories and play for 2-5 year olds and their parents. It's free, gentle, and a nice way to meet other local families.
tips: The latest library page says the sessions were paused and would return in autumn, so call 683 0970 or email kalamaja@tln.lib.ee to check dates and registration.

price.note: Free; registration may be needed as places are limited.

name: Estonian Children's Literature Centre
description: An Old Town house full of children's books, illustration galleries, and a fairytale attic on the top floor where kids can play and read. It runs toddler sessions and Saturday family mornings, so it's a cosy winter option.
tips: Groups and special sessions should be booked ahead by phone.

price.note: Entry policy for regular visits not confirmed.

hours: Weekdays 10:00-18:00, Sat 11:00-16:00 (autumn schedule from a third-party listing)

name: Mängu Saar Playroom
address: Päevalille tn 4, Tallinn (also Kopli tn 25 and Osmussaare tn 8)
description: A calm, Montessori-inspired indoor playroom with climbing areas and role-play corners that suits younger children better than big trampoline parks. Parents get seating where they can watch, and there's a small snack corner.
tips: You must buy a digital ticket for a time slot in advance, so don't just turn up.

price.note: Price not confirmed; prepaid digital ticket required.

name: Super Skypark (T1 Mall)
address: Peterburi tee 2, T1 Mall of Tallinn
description: A big trampoline and play centre on the top floor of T1 Mall, with a separate toddler area of mini trampolines and swings. It's loud and busy at peak times, so weekday mornings are best with a 1-2 year old.
tips: Children aged 7 and under must be supervised by a parent the whole time.

price.note: Child day passes reported from EUR 11 (third-party); under-3 price not confirmed.

discounts: Tallinn Card discount (also for up to 2 children aged 0-6 with an adult card holder)

name: Lohesaba Adventure City
description: An indoor play centre with a separate soft-play and developmental-games area for the smallest children. Adults get in free, which keeps a rainy-day visit cheap.
tips: No booking is needed for normal play visits.

price.note: Adults free; child price not confirmed.

name: Kalev Spa Water Park
description: A city-centre water park with a small children's pool with attractions, kids' slides, and a separate training pool, a good warm option in winter. It's walkable from the Old Town, so it's easy to combine with other plans.
tips: Go on a weekday, when the family pass is cheaper than at weekends.

price.note: Day ticket for children aged 1-6 EUR 6.80; family pass EUR 68 weekday / EUR 83 weekend (2 adults + up to 3 children). Adult price not confirmed; under-1s may be free (reseller info).

name: Ülemiste Centre
description: A large shopping centre with mother-and-baby rooms, free stroller hire, and the Lennumaa play area for small children. It's a practical rainy-day stop where you can run errands and let a toddler burn off energy.
tips: Parking is free for 5 hours, and there are wider family spaces near the entrance.

price.note: Free entry; play area pricing not confirmed.

name: Rätsepa Farm Animal Park
description: A farm west of Tallinn with goats, sheep, rabbits, poultry, and more unusual animals like kangaroos and ostriches, most of which you can pet. A guide introduces the animals, which toddlers usually love.
tips: Visits are by advance booking only, so contact info@ratsepa.ee or +372 529 9849 first.

price.note: Price not confirmed.
